nodes.name: β-Co(OH)2 synthesis
nodes.procedure: 45 mL of hexamethylenetetramine (HMT) (analytical reagent, AR) was dissolved into 800 mL of Milli-Q-grade ultrapure deionized water (DIW; ρ = 18.2 MΩ cm) and heated to 60°C under a N2 atmosphere with magnetic stirring. Subsequently, 20 mL of 2 mmol of CoCl2·6H2O (AR) aqueous solution was added dropwise into the HMT solution. The mixture was refluxed for 5 h under continuous magnetic stirring and N2 protection and then naturally cooled to room temperature without stirring. Thereafter, a pink precipitate was collected by centrifugation, washed successively with DIW and anhydrous ethanol, and dried overnight at 60°C under vacuum to obtain the catalyst precursor.

nodes.name: NDCO plasma treatment
nodes.procedure: To synthesize the NDCO catalyst, the precursor powder was treated with N2 plasma in the chamber of a radio frequency-plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition (RF-PECVD) system at a pressure of 0.02 Torr. Once the chamber reached the desired synthesis temperature, a radio frequency-plasma discharge of 200 W was carried out for 2 h to obtain NDCO.

nodes.name: CoO annealing
nodes.procedure: To synthesize the CoO catalyst, the precursor powder was placed inside the chamber and protected by an N2 atmosphere at a pressure of 0.02 Torr. Subsequently, the chamber temperature was raised to 200°C and annealed for 2 h to obtain the CoO catalyst.

nodes.name: CoN urea ammonolysis
nodes.procedure: To synthesize the CoN catalyst, the precursor powder and 1 g of urea powder (AR) were separately loaded into two ceramic boats, with the urea powder placed at the upstream side. Afterward, the samples were heated in an N2 atmosphere at a temperature of 400°C, with a heating rate of 5°C min⁻¹. After holding for 2 h, CoN powder was obtained.

nodes.description: OER performance in O2-saturated 1 M KOH using RDE

preconditioning.value: 30 cycles 1-1.6 V vs RHE at 100 mV/s

nodes.source_text: We assessed the electrocatalytic OER activity of NDCO by the RDE method at room temperature in an O₂-saturated 1 M KOH solution (pH = 14). The electrode was kept rotating at 1600 rpm... LSV in Figure 3a shows that the onset potential... is reduced by 172 mV after incorporating N into the CoO... At 10 mA cm⁻², NDCO requires an overpotential of 240 mV... Tafel slope of 75 mV dec⁻¹... j₀ of NDCO was determined to be 9.49 μA cm⁻²... TOF is 2634 h⁻¹ for NDCO... R_ct values of NDCO are much smaller than those of CoO and CoN

nodes.description: OER accelerated durability test (ADT) in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: the NDCO was subjected to an electrochemical accelerated deterioration test (ADT) under a sweep rate of 100 mV s⁻¹ between 1.0 and 1.6 V versus reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE)... exhibits negligible potential loss at 10 mA cm⁻² and mere ∼10 mV potential loss at 100 mA cm⁻² after 10,000 cycles.

nodes.description: OER chronopotentiometric stability at 10 mA/cm² in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: the galvanostatic stability test of NDCO was performed by holding the electrode current density constantly at 10 mA cm⁻². Figure 4g shows that the catalyst generally retained the initial electrode potential after 1000 h of aging, with a tiny degradation at an average rate of 0.03 mV h⁻¹... ICP-OES analysis... revealed that Co leaching from NDCO is negligible in a period of 500 h

nodes.description: AEMWE performance with NDCO anode and Pt/C cathode
nodes.source_text: We incorporated NDCO catalyst (3 mg_NDCO cm⁻²) in the anode... with 1 M KOH as the feed... the electrolyzer with an NDCO anode can reach this current density [1 A cm⁻²] at a voltage of a mere 1.78 V and... 2 A cm⁻² at 2.06 V (without cell iR correction)... galvanostatic stability test at... 1 A cm⁻²... no appreciable voltage increase over a 300-h continuous test at 60 °C... produced a total of 2.925 L of H₂... Faradaic efficiency of 99.95 %... energy consumption... 47.8 kWh/kg H₂

nodes.characterization_summary: NDCO inherits the hexagonal sheet-like morphology of β-Co(OH)₂ precursor but with increased surface roughness.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The resultant sample inherits the hexagonal sheet-like morphology of the β-Co(OH)₂ but with increased surface roughness when imaged by scanning electron microscopy (SEM) (Figure 2b,c).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM depicts the highly crystalline feature of NDCO with continuous lattice fringes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Atomic-resolution high-angle annular darkfield scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) depicts the highly crystalline feature of the sample with continuous lattice fringes (Figure 2d).

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM elemental mapping reveals uniform spatial distribution of Co, O, and N in NDCO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: STEM elemental mapping reveals a uniform spatial distribution of Co, O, and the ligands (Figure 2e).

nodes.characterization_summary: Powder XRD exhibits phase transformation of β-Co(OH)₂ precursor to cubic CoO (JCPDS 78-0431) for NDCO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Powder X-ray diffraction (XRD) in Figure 2f (red pattern) exhibits the phase transformation of β-Co(OH)₂ precursor to cubic CoO (JCPDS 78-0431).

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows characteristic Eg (480 cm⁻¹), F₂g (515 cm⁻¹), and A₁g (680 cm⁻¹) modes for CoO, majorly retained after N incorporation in NDCO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectroscopy measurements on CoO show clearly the characteristic Eg (480 cm⁻¹) F₂g (515 cm⁻¹) and A₁g (680 cm⁻¹) modes, which are majorly retained after N incorporation.

nodes.characterization_summary: KPFM shows work function of 4.63 eV for NDCO, 4.75 eV for CoO, and 4.69 eV for CoN.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The work function inferred from the experimental CPD values is 4.63 eV for NDCO versus 4.75 eV for CoO and 4.69 eV for CoN (Figure 2j).

nodes.characterization_summary: N 1s XPS shows three components: Co-N, N-Co-O, N-O bonds; O 1s shows Co-O, O-Co-N, O-N bonds with 0.2 eV negative shift of Co-O component; Co 2p analysis confirms N-doped CoO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoemission spectroscopy (XPS) measurements reveal that both N 1s and O 1s signals of the NDCO could be deconvoluted into three components attributed to Co-N, N-Co-O, and N-O bonds (Figure 2k) as well as Co-O, O-Co-N, and O-N bonds ... The negative shift (0.2 eV) of Co-O component in O 1s spectra ... These characteristic components further verify the formation of N-doped CoO, as echoed by the Co 3d core-level XPS analysis (Figure 2m).

nodes.characterization_summary: EXAFS at Co K-edge shows Co-N bond length of 1.38 Å and Co-O bond length of 1.61 Å in NDCO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Detailed analysis of R-space EXAFS spectroscopy of NDCO revealed two peaks at 1.38 and 1.61 Å, corresponding to Co-N and Co-O bonds, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES shows negligible Co leaching from NDCO after 500 h chronopotentiometry at 10 mA cm⁻².
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES) analysis of the electrolyte revealed that Co leaching from NDCO is negligible in a period of 500 h during the chronopotentimetry at 10 mA cm⁻² (Figure S18).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ EXAFS shows Co-O/N bond length reduction from ~1.59 Å to 1.48 Å under OER potentials, recoverable to ~1.58 Å at OCP; Co coordination number decreases with potential and recovers at OCP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: R-space spectra extracted from EXAFS show the reduction of BL_Co-O/N (from ~1.59 to 1.48 Å) in NDCO upon applying the OER potentials, which also can be recovered to the initial length of ~1.58 Å at the OCP (Figure 4g).
